newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nissan sees consolidated profit in 96/97 - paper.
newsitem.headline: Nissan sees consolidated profit in 96/97 - paper.

text.p: Nissan Motor Co Ltd will show a profit on a consolidated basis in the year ending in March, a Japanese business daily reported on Tuesday.
The Nihon Keizai Shimbun said the company is expected to post a consolidated net profit of about 55 billion yen, compared with a net loss of 88.4 billion yen the previous year.
A Nissan spokeswoman on Tuesday morning declined to comment on the report.

The newspaper said the main reason for the improvement was because the company's manufacturing and sales subsidiary in Mexico was expected to have turned a profit of about 30 billion yen after posting a net loss of about 35 billion yen in calendar 1995.

The paper also said that losses at Nissan's European operations were expected have shrunk to approximately 45 billion yen in calendar 1996 from 65 billion yen in 1995, thanks to restructuring efforts and the yen's decline against the dollar.
Also, net profits at the company's U.S. operations were expected to have doubled to more than 20 billion yen, the paper said.
Nissan's parent current profits for the 1996/97 business year are expected to reach 80 billion yen, up 150 percent from the previous year, the newspaper said.
